title: Bootcamp-hosted-api-screens-and-snippets
creator: Ava Chen
body:
Summary:
This ticket delivers a compact, task-focused screenshot and visual asset suite for the Hosted API getting-started flow. The goal is to replace lengthy, ambiguous onboarding images with a small set of high-utility screenshots and annotated snippets that demonstrate: model selection, a guided request-builder, immediate copyable code in three languages, and clear error/edge-state handling for new users.

Design goals:
- Make the first 90 seconds after signup feel productive: users can select a model, craft a single request, and run sample code.
- Surface choices that affect cost/latency (model family, max_tokens, temperature) without overwhelming the user.
- Provide short, copyable snippets (cURL / Python / JS) alongside a visual request builder so non-CLI users can get started.
- Illustrate graceful fallbacks and region/model variant hints for reliability.

Assets delivered (high level):
- Model card compact view (hostedapi_modelcard_compact.png): focuses on 3 key metrics (latency median, cost per 1k tokens, recommended use cases) and a single-click "Try with sample prompt" CTA.
- Guided request builder flow (request_builder_flow.png): 4-frame storyboard showing: (1) pick a prompt template, (2) toggle presets (fast/cost-efficient/accurate), (3) preview tokens and estimated cost, (4) run and view live streaming response.
- Code snippets tile (code_snippets_dark.png): ready-to-copy examples for cURL, Python (requests + streaming example), and Node (fetch + streaming) each with inline comments highlighting where to paste API key and where to adjust model params.
- Error & edge states collage (error_states_collage.png): empty-key placeholder, rate-limit toast, model-unavailable fallback showing "switch to compatible variant" CTA.
- Figma source file with component variants and export-ready frames (figma:Bootcamp_HostedAPI_Screens_v3).

Unique UX elements (not in existing assets):
- Preset toggles that visually change an estimated latency/cost meter in real time (visual affordance for trade-offs).
- A tiny inline 'compatibility hint' under each model entry showing which downstream features are supported (streaming, function-calls, structured-output).
- Compact code tile that syncs with the request builder: when a user changes a parameter the code updates visually so screenshots can demonstrate mutable code. This asset was photographed in three states for docs: default, changed-temperature, changed-max_tokens.

Accessibility and localization notes:
- All screenshot text uses 16px+ font sizes and 4.5:1 contrast for primary CTA text.
- Where color communicates state (latency meter), we include iconography and text labels so information isn't color-dependent.
- Text placeholders and CTA labels in assets prepared for English and will be passed to localization with spacing notes.

Review feedback captured so far:
- PM (Riley Alvarez): request builder copy should call out "estimated cost" rather than "price" to avoid legal phrasing. Updated.
- Engineering (Lina Gomez): streaming example must include explicit chunk-handling pseudo-code. Added the short snippet and a link to detailed streaming sample in docs PR.
- Security (Devon Roy): ensure screenshots redact API key placeholders and do not display real telemetry. Confirmed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Screenshots exported at 2x and 3x at both light and dark theme.
- All code snippet text is selectable in the docs site and matches the exported tile.
- Figma file contains component tokens and four annotated frames with callouts for engineers (export name, intended viewport, assets to generate).
- Design review completed and signoff from PM and ENG.

Links to artifacts and next steps:
- Figma file: figma.com/file/Bootcamp_HostedAPI_Screens_v3 (internal).
- Docs PR with screenshots attached: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/472.
- Console PR to add image gallery to the onboarding modal: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-console/pull/1832.
- Next: coordinate with content writer to produce short alt-text strings and microcopy variants for A/B test (see sub-issue DES-24792).

Notes for engineers implementing screenshots into the docs site:
- Use the compact model card image for the top-of-flow hero with HTML alt text: "Compact model selection card showing latency, cost estimate, and Try button".
- When embedding the code tile, prefer the selectable inline snippet and fallback to a download PNG only for PDF exports.
- Respect recommended viewport 1200x700 when placing multi-column images to avoid reflow.

Designer handoff checklist (completed):
- [x] Figma frames exported (2x / 3x)
- [x] Dark mode variants exported
- [x] Annotated spec doc for developers linked in PR
- [x] Accessibility contrast check performed

Signoffs: Ava Chen (Design lead), Riley Alvarez (PM), Lina Gomez (Staff Engineer).
ux_notes: Prefer short captions under each screenshot that describe the user action (e.g., 'Pick a model — try the sample prompt'). Keep microcopy to < 100 characters per caption. For code snippets include inline comments for 'where to insert API key' and a one-line explanation of expected response shape.
acceptance_criteria: all images exported in light/dark at 2x & 3x
code snippets copyable and match docs PR
Figma contains annotated frames and component tokens
PM and ENG signoff captured in comments
